interfaces.name: Root air drying
interfaces.function: Assemble a reusable stone-and-bark tray, process actual roots and allow weather-dependent drying with reversible preservation while sufficiently dry.
interfaces.costs: Build: two stone units and one bark, two rounds at one energy. Load: up to two original root units, two crushing rounds per raw root at one energy. Already crushed compatible food needs one transfer round, with its prior costs and composition preserved. Unload/dismantle: one round and one energy. Passive weather exchange costs no actor rounds.
interfaces.effects: Food begins at its represented composition or the reviewed 50% root water assumption. Uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per root per round to fraction 0.12; rain returns up to 0.01 per root, capped at original water. At fraction <=0.12 decay is 0.35 baseline, otherwise crushed food is 1.25 baseline. Exposure continues after unloading. No lost nutrients, reverse spoilage, sterilization or free materials.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

personalIntent.goal: Maintain safe food supplies and test whether root preservation is practical locally.
personalIntent.reason: Root air drying is mastered, but no stone or bark is currently available in my inventory or visible ground stacks.
personalIntent.progress: Two roots remain. The drying contract requires two stone units and one bark; its preservation benefit depends on prolonged dry conditions.
personalIntent.next: Ask a nearby participant about materials, recover energy, and inspect the nearby tree without assuming it supplies bark.

shown.question: Can root air drying reduce food loss under local conditions?
evidence: Root air drying is personally mastered.
The contract requires two stone units and one bark for a reusable tray.
Drying is slow and rain reverses water loss; preservation applies only at water fraction at or below 0.12.
Two roots are currently carried; no stone or bark is carried.
shown.uncertainty: Sources of stone and bark and practical drying time in local weather remain unverified.
shown.goal: Evaluate a feasible safe food reserve without wasting food or excessive effort.
completedSteps: Completed study of root air drying.
outputs: Personal mastery of root air drying.
shown.missing: Actual tray materials and evidence of useful drying under local weather.
shown.next: Seek material-source information and inspect a nearby tree.
shown.benefit: No preservation benefit has yet been demonstrated.

shown.subject: Local material sightings
shown.text: Have you actually seen any stone or bark sources nearby? I read the root-processing contracts: crushing alone does not preserve roots, and air drying requires two stone units, one bark and sustained dry weather. I am scouting a short distance east.

shown.subject: Root drying materials
shown.text: I have not identified stone or bark sources. I have mastered drying but have no tray materials. I will seek a way to survey actual accessible materials; please share what your tree inspection actually finds. No tray has been built by me.

shown: Known roots provide 14 nutrition with zero toxicity; food does not heal.
No stone or bark source has yet been verified.
Do not crush carried food before a practical drying setup is available.

shown.description: Read a retained personal record index page.
